# Adjudication Task — Chapter 632

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃632화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|내궁(內宮).
  6|
  7|현재 머무르고 있는 처소도 내궁에 속한 곳이지만, 야율목이 말하고자 하는 뜻이 그게 아니라는 것쯤은 곧장 알아차릴 수 있었다.
  8|
  9|“야율 대협이 우리를?”
 10|
 11|“그래. 정확히는 너와 그 노인만 데려오라 이르셨다.”
 12|
 13|좋은 소식이다. 그간 묵묵부답으로 일관하던 야수묘왕이 마침내 내 독대 요청에 응했다는 거니까.
 14|
 15|하지만 화룡각 전체도 아니고 나와 남호, 단 두 사람만 콕 집어 부르다니.
 16|
 17|그 순간 의문과 함께 뇌리를 스쳐 지나가는 어떤 생각에, 나는 문득 입을 열었다.
 18|
 19|“다른 사람의 이목을 피해야 하나?”
 20|
 21|의외라는 표정으로 나를 빤히 바라보던 야율목이 작게 고개를 끄덕인다.
 22|
 23|“생각보다 눈치가 빠르군. 가급적이면 눈에 띄지 않게 움직여야 한다.”
 24|
 25|“바로 내일이 부족 대회의니까?”
 26|
 27|“아니, 대부분의 부족장들이 너희를 싫어하니까.”
 28|
 29|“…….”
 30|
 31|“사실이다.”
 32|
 33|혹시 전생에 기요틴이었나. 뒤에 나올 말까지 싹둑 잘라 내는 것 보소.
 34|
 35|그래도 부정할 수 없는 사실이라 나는 씁쓸하게 입맛을 다셨다.
 36|
 37|“대충 사정은 알겠네. 야율 대협도 이곳저곳에서 압박을 받고 있는 모양이지?”
 38|
 39|뭐라 말할 것처럼 입술을 달싹이던 야율목이 이내 굳은 얼굴로 입을 다문다.
 40|
 41|내가 앞서 들었던 말을 부정하지 못했듯이, 녀석도 마찬가지였다.
 42|
 43|하지만 인정할 건 인정해야 하는 법.
 44|
 45|남만은 중원인들의 편견처럼 야만스러운 땅이 아니며, 야수묘왕은 왕이 아니라 그들을 대표하는 대족장 중 한 사람일 뿐이었다.
 46|
 47|‘나도 아는 사실을, 이 녀석이 모를 리는 없지.’
 48|
 49|야율목은 나름대로 괜찮은 녀석이지만 아직 치기(稚氣)를 완전히 벗지 못한 청년이기도 하다.
 50|
 51|그리고 그때, 자존심이 상한 표정으로 입을 꾹 다물고 있던 야율목이 작게 중얼거렸다.
 52|
 53|“네놈의 말이 맞다. 제아무리 아버님이라 해도, 홀로 그들을 감당하시는 건 무리야.”
 54|
 55|“……?”
 56|
 57|“뭐냐, 그 표정은?”
 58|
 59|“아니, 그냥 의외라서. 이렇게 솔직하게 말할 줄은 몰랐지. 그새 철 좀 들었구나?”
 60|
 61|이틀 전 나누었던 대화로 뭔가 깨달은 게 있나?
 62|
 63|그러고 보면 여전히 사춘기 중학생처럼 틱틱거리긴 해도 꼬박꼬박 멧돼지도 직접 잡아다 주는 등, 야율목은 처음보다는 훨씬 호의적인 태도를 보였다.
 64|
 65|‘그렇다면 좋은 일이지. 이 넓은 땅덩어리에 우리 편이 좁쌀만큼이라는 게 문제지만.’
 66|
 67|나는 발끈한 얼굴을 한 야율목보다 한발 빨리 입을 열었다.
 68|
 69|“시간과 장소는?”
 70|
 71|“인시(寅時). 그때 데리러 오지.”
 72|
 73|“좋아. 아, 그리고 기왕 오는 김에…….”
 74|
 75|“오는 김에. 뭐?”
 76|
 77|“사슴이나 노루 좀 잡아 와. 멧돼지 말고.”
 78|
 79|“……!”
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|* * *
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|무림에서의 하루는 열두 시진으로 나뉘고, 한 시진은 두 시간을 뜻하며 인시는 새벽 세 시부터 다섯 시까지의 시각을 의미한다.
 88|
 89|그리고 야율목은 약속을 지켰다. 모두가 깊은 잠에 빠진 새벽, 전신이 새하얀 털로 뒤덮인 백호 한 마리가 어둠을 가르고 처소 앞에 내려앉았다.
 90|
 91|쿵.
 92|
 93|낯익은 모습으로 죽어 있는 한 마리의 짐승도 함께.
 94|
 95|“시벌, 또 멧돼지네. 너 일부러 이러지?”
 96|
 97|“오다 주웠다.”
 98|
 99|“자꾸 줍긴 뭘 주워. 혹시 멧돼지 밭이라도 있냐? 물만 주면서 쑥쑥 키우다가 서리해 와?”
100|
101|남호가 어리둥절한 표정으로 물었다.
102|
103|“서리가 뭔가? 난생처음 들어보는데.”
104|
105|“그런 게 있어요. 남 노인한테는 난생처음이 아니라, 어차피 이번 생에는 두 번 다시 못 들어볼 겁니다.”
106|
107|“역시 한족 놈이라 그런지 말하는 꼬락서니가…….”
108|
109|“한족 혐오를 멈춰 주세요.”
110|
111|언짢은 목소리로 투덜거리는 남호에게 정중한 중단 요청을 넣은 내게, 야율목이 자신의 뒷자리를 턱짓했다.
112|
113|“타라.”
114|
115|“이 호랑이를?”
116|
117|“……그럼 내가 목말이라도 태워 줘야 하나?”
118|
119|“성깔 있어 보이는데.”
120|
121|“편견이다. 새끼 때부터 함께한 녀석이라 순하기 그지없지. 정 못 믿겠으면 시험해 보든가.”
122|
123|“오. 그래?”
124|
125|나는 백호의 턱을 쓰다듬기 위해 손을 뻗었……다가 번개처럼 뒤로 뺐다.
126|
127|딱!
128|
129|크고 날카로운 이빨이 허공을 갈랐다. 떨떠름한 얼굴로 대답을 요구하는 내 눈빛에, 야율목이 작게 입맛을 다셨다.
130|
131|“아쉽군.”
132|
133|“시벌놈이.”
134|
135|“못 믿겠으면 시험해 보라고 했지. 안 문다는 말은 안 했다.”
136|
137|개도 안 믿을 헛소리를 지껄인 야율목이 백호의 미간을 살살 긁었다.
138|
139|“야호. 야호야. 성내지 말거라.”
140|
141|갑자기 저러길래 처음에는 북한산 등산객 코스프레인 줄 알았는데, 문득 머릿속에 떠오르는 생각이 있었다.
142|
143|“그거 설마 저 녀석 이름이냐?”
144|
145|야율목이 당당하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
146|
147|“무야호(武野虎). 굳센 벌판의 호랑이라는 뜻이다.”
148|
149|“…….”
150|
151|“참으로 멋있는 이름이지. 그렇지 않나?”
152|
153|그릉. 그르릉.
154|
155|꼴에 자기도 고양이과라고, 골골송을 부르는 백호를 귀여워 죽겠다는 눈빛으로 바라본 야율목이 자랑스럽게 말을 이었다.
156|
157|“그만큼 기분이 좋다는 거다. 이제 올라타도 좋아.”
158|
159|“……아, 으응.”
160|
161|“표정이 왜 그러지? 무슨 문제라도 있나?”
162|
163|있지. 나만 알고 있는 약간의 문제가. 근데 여기서는 말 못 하지.
164|
165|목구멍까지 차오른 말을 삼킨 나는 잠자코 백호의 등에 올라탔고, 이어 약간 상기된 얼굴을 한 남호가 그 뒤를 이었다.
166|
167|“내가 이 나이에 전사들에게만 허락된다는 호랑이를 타 볼 줄이야. 그것도 신령스러운 백호를!”
168|
169|원래 이 세상에 내 새끼 칭찬만큼 기쁜 게 없다. 야호맘 야율목이 뿌듯한 표정으로 고개를 끄덕였다.
170|
171|“역시 노인장께서 뭘 아시는군. 백호를 좋아하시오?”
172|
173|“아, 그럼. 내가 평소에도 많이 좋아하지.”
174|
175|“…….”
176|
177|아냐, 그만해. 거기까지 하는 건 무리수야.
178|
179|기대 반, 우려 반으로 뒤이어 나올 대사를 기다리던 그때.
180|
181|사람 셋을 태우고도 아무렇지 않게 기지개를 쭉 켠 백호가 지면을 박차고 달려나갔다.
182|
183|파파팟!
184|
185|그렇게 밝은 달빛 아래. 어두운 밀림을 빛살처럼 가로지르던 삼인일호(三人一虎)의 걸음이 멈춘 곳은 무너져 가는 낡은 사당이었다.
186|
187|
188|
189|* * *
190|
191|
192|
193|사당 안의 공기는 습식 사우나 안처럼 후텁지근했다.
194|
195|먼지가 쌓인 바닥과 벌레가 좀 먹은 기둥, 금방이라도 꺼질 것처럼 휘청이는 호롱불은 내부를 흐릿하게 밝히고 있었다.
196|
197|그리고 그 모든 것의 중심에, 우리를 기다리고 있던 한 사람이 있었다.
198|
199|“오랜만에 와 보니 엉망이더군. 하긴, 그때도 영 좋은 상태는 아니었지.”
200|
201|처음 만났을 때와 달리, 낮은 뇌까림과 함께 돌아선 야수묘왕 야율척의 표정은 호롱불의 불빛처럼 흐릿했고, 그 안에는 숨길 수 없는 피로가 엿보였다.
202|
203|그런 이유에서였을까. 나를 포함한 그 누구도 묻지 않았다. 왜 내궁의 대전(大殿)이 아닌 낡은 사당에서 우리를 만나는지에 대해서.
204|
205|그 대신 나는, 두서없는 그의 말을 받아 주는 것을 택했다.
206|
207|“언제를 말씀하시는 겁니까?”
208|
209|“젊었을 때지. 아니, 젊다 못해 어렸던 시절이었어. 도저히 수습할 수 없는 대형 사고를 친 날이면, 우리는 늘 어른들을 피해 이곳에 숨어 있었다.”
210|
211|“우리라면…….”
212|
213|“너도 이미 만난 적 있는 자다. 이미 짐작하고 있겠지만.”
214|
215|“백상(白象)이군요. 백족의 대족장.”
216|
217|야수묘왕이 고개를 끄덕였다.
218|
219|“맞다. 바로 그다.”
220|
221|“오랜 시간을 함께했다는 건 알고 있습니다.”
222|
223|“오랜 시간이라는 표현으로도 부족하다. 그야말로 일평생을 함께 했으니. 목초지에서, 늪에서, 산과 들. 그리고 전장에서까지도 우리는 함께였다.”
224|
225|잠시 그때를 생각하는 듯, 흔들리는 호롱불을 말없이 응시하던 야수묘왕이 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
226|
227|“그래. 그렇고말고.”
228|
229|“두 분이고 떼 놓을 수 없는 죽마고우이자 의형제라고 들었습니다.”
230|
231|불쑥 내뱉은 말에 야수묘왕의 시선이 내게 옮겨 간다. 나는 그의 눈을 똑바로 바라보며 말을 이었다.
232|
233|“그런데, 지금도 그렇습니까?”
234|
235|“음.”
236|
237|“……진태경. 입조심해라.”
238|
239|크르릉.
240|
241|웅크리고 있던 백호가 낮은 울음소리를 토해 낸다.
242|
243|나직한 경고와 함께 앞으로 나선 자신의 아들을 향해, 작게 손을 내저어 보인 야수묘왕이 나를 물끄러미 응시했다.
244|
245|“아니라고 생각하느냐?”
246|
247|“그냥 문득 그런 생각이 들었습니다. 백상 대족장의 생각은 궁주님과 다를 것 같다는 생각이.”
248|
249|“…….”
250|
251|“얼마나 자세히 아시는지는 모르겠지만, 지금 중원에서는 별의별 일이 다 일어나고 있습니다. 그중에서도 첫 시작은 저희 태원진가가 있는 산서성이었고요.”
252|
253|지금까지도 생생한 기억이다.
254|
255|소림혈사, 사천혈사 등의 굵직한 사건에 의해 가려져 있지만, 암천이라는 이름이 처음 중원에 모습을 등장한 것은 바로 산서성에서였다.
256|
257|항산검문과 대장로를 조종하여 전쟁을 벌였고, 자그마치 일천에 달하는 사람들이 목숨을 잃어야만 했다.
258|
259|‘은영각에서 정보를 전달받았다면, 모를 수가 없겠지.’
260|
261|그리고 내 생각을 읽은 것처럼 야수묘왕은 고개를 끄덕였다.
262|
263|“이미 들어서 알고 있다. 화양검 진백양과는 일면식도 나눈 사이였고.”
264|
265|“그 누구도 예상치 못했습니다. 가문에 속하지 않은 외인(外人)이라면 모를까. 대장로는 피로 이어진 혈육이자 태원진가의 큰 어른이었으니까요.”
266|
267|그건 진위경이 대장로를 경계하면서도 끝까지 믿었던 이유이기도 했고, 야수묘왕은 내 말의 의미를 알아차리지 못할 만큼 둔감한 사내가 아니었다.
268|
269|“백상은…… 아니다. 그럴 리 없다. 그는 화양검과 달라.”
270|
271|“그건 누구도 모릅니다.”
272|
273|단호한 내 대답에 이어, 묵묵히 상황을 지켜보던 남호가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
274|
275|“오래전 혈육처럼 아끼던 수하가 있었소. 그는 몰락한 무가(武家)의 유일한 후손이었고, 부모는 마교에 의해 살해당했지. 훗날 서쪽에서 십만 마도라는 들불이 일어나자 그는 무림맹에 투신했소. 늘 죽음을 두려워하지 않고 작전에 임했기에 그가 가져온 정보들로 십여 차례의 작은 승리를 가져올 수 있었지.”
276|
277|나조차도 들은 적 없던, 세상에 알려지지 않은 어느 은영각 요원의 이야기다.
278|
279|그러나 남호의 어두운 표정처럼, 곧이어 이어진 말들도 그러했다.
280|
281|“일이 벌어진 후에도 믿을 수 없었소. 그가 배신자라는 것을. 어느 날 그가 팔 하나와 바꿔 가져온 정보가, 오천여 명의 맹원(盟員)을 사지로 내몰리라는 것을.”
282|

Dust coated the floor. Insects had eaten into the pillars. An oil lamp wavered as though it might go out at any moment, casting a dim light through the room.

[P90]
At the center of it all, someone was waiting for us.

[P91]
“I hadn’t been back in so long, I found the place a mess. Then again, it wasn’t in very good shape back then either.”

[P92]
The Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok, turned toward us. Unlike when we’d first met, his expression was as faint as the lamplight, though the weariness in it was plain to see.

[P93]
Perhaps that was why none of us asked why he’d chosen to meet us in an old shrine rather than the Inner Palace’s main hall. Instead, I took up the thread of his wandering thoughts.

[P94]
“When was that?”

[P95]
“When I was young. No, younger than young. We were children. Whenever we caused a disaster too big to put right, we hid here from the adults.”

[P96]
“We?”

[P97]
“You’ve met him. I imagine you’ve already guessed.”

[P98]
“Baeksang. Great chieftain of the Bai people.”

[P99]
The Beast Miao King nodded. “That’s right. Him.”

[P100]
“I know you’ve been together a long time.”

[P101]
“A long time doesn’t cover it. We spent our whole lives together. In the grasslands, in the swamps, across mountains and fields—even on the battlefield.”

[P102]
He gazed silently at the wavering lamp for a moment, as though looking back on those days, then gave a small nod.

[P103]
“Yes. We did.”

[P104]
“I heard you were inseparable childhood friends and sworn brothers.”

[P105]
His eyes moved to me. I met his gaze and went on.

[P106]
“Are you still?”

[P107]
“Hmm.”

[P108]
“……Jin Taekyung. Watch your mouth.”

[P109]
*Grrrr.*

[P110]
The crouching White Tiger let out a low growl. The Beast Miao King waved a hand at his son, who had stepped forward to warn me, and studied my face.

[P111]
“You think we aren’t?”

[P112]
“It occurred to me that Great Chieftain Baeksang might not see things the way you do, Palace Lord.”

[P113]
“……”

[P114]
“I don’t know how much you’ve heard, but all sorts of things are happening in the Central Plains. It started in Shanxi Province, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan is.”

[P115]
I remembered it vividly.

[P116]
The Shaolin Bloodshed and the Sichuan Blood Tragedy had since overshadowed it, but Dark Heaven had first made its appearance in the Central Plains in Shanxi Province. They had manipulated the Mount Heng Sword Sect and the Head Elder into waging war. Nearly a thousand people had lost their lives.

[P117]
*If the Hidden Shadow Pavilion has been keeping him informed, he has to know.*

[P118]
As though he’d read my mind, the Beast Miao King nodded.

[P119]
“I’ve heard. I’d met the Blade of Flowers, Jin Baekyang, myself.”

[P120]
“No one saw it coming. It might have been different if he’d been an outsider with no ties to the family. But the Head Elder was our blood kin, one of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most senior members.”

[P121]
That was why Jin Wikyung had trusted the Head Elder to the end despite his suspicions. The Beast Miao King was sharp enough to understand what I was getting at.

[P122]
“Baeksang… No. It can’t be. He’s not like the Blade of Flowers.”

[P123]
“No one knows that.”

[P124]
Namho, who had been watching in silence, spoke up.

[P125]
“Long ago, I had a subordinate I cherished like family. He was the last descendant of a fallen martial family. The Demonic Cult had killed his parents. Later, when a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path rose like wildfire in the west, he joined the Murim Alliance. He never feared death on a mission, and the information he brought back won us more than ten small victories.”

[P126]
I’d never heard of this Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent. Neither had the rest of the world.

[P127]
Namho’s face darkened, and so did the story.

[P128]
“Even after it happened, I couldn’t believe he was a traitor. One day, he sacrificed an arm to bring us information. That information sent more than five thousand Alliance members into the jaws of death.”

[P129]
“……!”

[P130]
“When the truth came out, he fled. A few days later, a squad sent to kill him brought back a man’s head. He was grinning from ear to ear. I wonder what had made him so happy.”

[P131]
His voice faded into silence. Namho sighed deeply before he spoke again.

[P132]
“This old man isn’t saying the Bai great chieftain serves Dark Heaven. But this is Murim. We can’t see an inch ahead of us. Baeksang. Yohi. Heugung. Or one of the thirty-two tribal chiefs gathering here tomorrow. I wouldn’t be surprised if any one of them turned out to be a traitor.”

[P133]
For a long time, the Beast Miao King said nothing. He watched the oil lamp sway and right itself, over and over, before turning back to me.

[P134]
“Are you certain?”

[P135]
“Of one thing, at least.”

[P136]
“What?”

[P137]
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress. That fucking bitch won’t leave Nanman alone.”

[P138]
The Beast Miao King let out a low groan.

[P139]
“Nanman is no easy target.”

[P140]
“Were the Sichuan Tang Clan, Shaolin Temple, Emei Sect, and Qingcheng Sect easy fucking pushovers, then?”

[P141]
“……!”

[P142]
“Uh. Sorry. That came out harsher than I meant.”

[P143]
The Beast Miao King gave a startled laugh at my outburst.

[P144]
“You really are Old Master Jeok’s disciple.”

[P145]
“He’d be offended if he heard you say that.”

[P146]
“He’d secretly love it.”

[P147]
“……Oh.”

[P148]
*Okay. He knows Old Man Jeok.*

[P149]
I was giving him a mental thumbs-up when a sudden rush of movement came from outside the shrine.

[P150]
*Whoosh, hiss!*

[P151]
A voice followed, held as low as its owner could manage.

[P152]
“P-Palace Lord!”

[P153]
At the same moment, a red warning light went off in my head.

[P154]
And a System alert sounded.

[P155]
> **System**
>
> *Ding.*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
